newsitem.title: USA: U.S. justice calls affirmative action difficult.
newsitem.headline: U.S. justice calls affirmative action difficult.

text.p: Supreme Court Justice Stephen Breyer said Thursday that affirmative action to help minorities or women has emerged as an extremely difficult issue for him.

"To what extent should there be affirmative action, which can take people who haven't had a good chance in life and give them an opportunity and when does it go too far so that it is actually depriving a person who is not a minority...of a fair chance?" he asked.

"That is not an easy question to answer, either as a matter of morals, as a matter of policy or as a matter of law," Breyer said in a discussion with high school students broadcast by the cable television company C-SPAN.
Breyer noted the Supreme Court often has split by a 5-4 vote on the issue of affirmative action programmes designed to help minorities and women overcome past discrimination.
"You can see by the closeness of it what a difficult issue it is," he said.
Breyer, who was named to the high court by President Clinton, has been in the minority among those more liberal justices who have supported affirmative action.
In other comments, Breyer said cases were decided "based on the law and the arguments" and the outcome was not influenced by news stories or opinion polls.

He also said he tried not to get emotionally involved in the cases, but sought to make reasoned arguments. "I've found the more emotional you are, the less persuasive you are," Breyer said of his discussions with the other justices.
